scope: Theorem 7.6 (The sharp marked-pair bound) of the manuscript “Marked polygon correlations and one-arc bounds” (preprints/Marked-polygon-correlations-and-one-arc-bounds-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 acb3276f993c6d8e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 51. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix c1 ∈ (0, 1] and a sufficiently small c4 > 0. Consider the physical cyclic row [p, X, p′, Y ] with s = |X|, b = |Y |, and N = s + b + 2 even. All real site offsets vanish. Ordinary Y sites have height zero; ordinary X sites and both marks have heights in {0, β}. Let t be the upper-height fraction in X and set LX = γ−1 log s, LY = γ−1 log b. Uniformly as LY → ∞ under c1LY ≤ LX ≤ LY , 1 2 ≤ t ≤ 1, t < 1 =⇒ s(1 − t) ≥ ec4LY , one has log C(p, p′ ) ≤ − 4 3 log s + 617 1200 log(b/s) + o(log b).
